thread:
customer_jane: Hey team — after we rolled out device-trust for our Okta SSO yesterday some users are getting immediately logged out and API calls that use the session cookie return 401. Happening across Chrome + Safari. Any ideas?

lina_support: sorry to hear that! quick Qs: are they using the web console or API clients? can you paste repro steps and one failing cookie header (sanitized ok)? also which env (prod/stage) and a sample user id?

customer_jane: Repro on prod. Steps: 1) login via SSO 2) enable device-trust on user in org admin 3) reload app -> instant redirect to /login. curl to our session-check endpoint: 

```bash
curl -i -H "Cookie: rdw_session=eyJhbGciOi..." https://api.customer-app.com/_session_check
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"session_invalid","reason":"session_binding_mismatch"}
```

We also see browser console: 
`Set-Cookie: rdw_session=; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; Path=/; Domain=.customer-app.com`

matt_auth: pinging in. thanks for the detail @lina_support @customer_jane. initial read: error `session_binding_mismatch` suggests the server considers the session bound to a previous device key and now fails validation. can you confirm the jwt payload (sanitized) for rdw_session contains a `device_key_id` claim? also any reverse-proxy logs for Set-Cookie from auth service?

customer_jane: payload includes `device_key_id: "dk_abc123"`. reverse-proxy logs show auth set-cookie as `rdw_session=...; SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; Domain=.customer-app.com` — but the value is blank when the client gets it. not seeing HttpOnly flag in the set line (browser devtools shows HttpOnly though).

priya_infra: quick hypothesis: when device-trust was toggled we rotate the device binding and immediately invalidate existing sessions. there should be a grace window of 5 minutes but maybe env var was set to 0 in prod during the rollout. can someone check `DEVICE_TRUST_GRACE` on auth-prod? if that's 0 that explains immediate sign-outs.

lina_support: @priya_infra can you also check redis TTL for sessions? sample redis key seen in logs: `session:user:98765`.

priya_infra: checking... 
`$ redis-cli -h auth-redis GET session:user:98765` -> returns token id, TTL says 0 secs (expired). Uh.

matt_auth: hmm. digging into auth-server logs for that user: 
```
INFO 2026-11-04T14:22:01Z auth-session refresh requested user=98765 device_key=dk_abc123
WARN 2026-11-04T14:22:02Z device-trust rotation for user=98765 applied, grace_window=0
ERROR 2026-11-04T14:22:02Z session binding mismatch: expected=dk_abc123 got=dk_def456
```

matt_auth: that log shows grace_window=0. two things to do: 1) short-term workaround set grace window >0 so existing sessions not invalidated immediately 2) root fix is a regression in the device-trust rollout script that accidentally set grace to 0 for new orgs.

lina_support: customer_jane — can we do a coordinated quick patch? we can set DEVICE_TRUST_GRACE=300 on auth-prod and rotate sessions more gracefully. alternatively admin action: force reauth for affected users via Admin Console (that will nudge customers, but might be disruptive). which do you prefer?

customer_jane: they need minimal disruption. if setting grace window avoids forced logins that's best. can you outline exact steps so we can confirm on a small subset?

priya_infra: steps to test on a single user (non-prod first):
1) create test user with device-trust enabled
2) issue session (curl login)
3) toggle device-trust via okta API (simulate rotation)
4) confirm session still accepted within grace window

Script (example):
```bash
# create session
curl -X POST https://auth.customer-app.com/login -d '{"username":"test+dt@example.com"}' -c /tmp/cookiejar
# toggle device trust (okta-admin token needed)
curl -X POST "https://okta.example.com/api/v1/users/test+dt@example.com/credentials/device-trust" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OKTA_ADMIN"
# check session
curl -b /tmp/cookiejar https://api.customer-app.com/_session_check -i
```

matt_auth: and to patch on prod quickly we can flip DEVOPS flag: `DEVICE_TRUST_GRACE=300` on the auth-prod deployment, reload config, and monitor. I can prepare a hotfix to set default to 300 and also add a safety rollout check.

security-bot: alert: multiple session invalidations detected for org=acct-42 during rollout. creating incident record INC-2026-824.

lina_support: raised ticket RED-INC-2026-824 and looped in security and eng. @matt_auth can you do the hotfix? @priya_infra can you update redis TTLs if needed?

matt_auth: patch in review, deploying now. hotfix changes default grace window and adds telemetry when grace==0.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for auth-service-prod (hotfix/device-trust-grace).

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded - auth-service-prod v2026.11.04-hotfix-1 — rollout 3/3 nodes.

matt_auth: done. I also set `DEVICE_TRUST_GRACE=300` in prod env and forced a config reload. watching metrics: session invalidation spikes dropping.

priya_infra: ran redis script to refresh TTLs for active sessions in the last 15m: 
```
# extend TTL by 300s for active sessions
for k in $(redis-cli -h auth-redis KEYS "session:user:*"); do redis-cli -h auth-redis EXPIRE $k 300; done
```

customer_jane: confirming — on my end users are staying logged in after toggling device-trust now. thank you all for the quick turnaround. we'll keep an eye and report any residuals. really appreciate the fast fix. :heart:

lina_support: marking as resolved for now, will keep incident open for postmortem. next steps: postmortem + update rollout script to not set grace=0.

matt_auth: i'll open PR with test coverage for grace window and add a canary flag for device-trust rollouts.

customer_jane: thanks everyone. if anything else pops up I'll reopen thread.
